subject: Mutual action plan: latency & throughput SLOs — next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aarti Shah <aarti.shah@neptunehealth.com>, DKim Patel <dkpatel@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-11T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Mutually agreed next steps from today's deep-dive

Hi Aarti / DKim —

Thanks again for a productive deep-dive today. Below is my read of the things we agreed on plus open asks. Please correct any mistakes.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Real-time triage service must respond within 60ms P95 for single-shot inference on short prompts (document classification + routing).
- Batch clinical summarization jobs must sustain ~1200 reqs/hour with median completion under 2s per request (these are queued batch flows from overnight ingestion).
- Strict data governance: model outputs must be retained only for 7 days and audit logs should be available to your security team.

Technical commitments (high level):
1) Model selection: Redwood will validate two candidate model families that match your precision/latency tradeoff — an 8-bit quantized LLaMA-family variant and a distilled instruction-tuned decoder with sparse attention. We will run the benchmark on your 512-token typical context and a 2048-token worst case.
2) SLO targets we scoped: 60ms P95 for short-shot routing; 250ms P99 for 2048-token generative flows; throughput targets per pool: 300 concurrent small requests / 1x batch lane for summarization (scaling plan described below).
3) Topology: hybrid routing — edge-prefetch (region: us-west) -> regional serving pool (dedicated) -> fallback to hosted burst capacity. Can support private VPC peering for production traffic.
4) Security/compliance: KMS integration and audit stream export (we'll provide schema for logs).

Open asks / action items (owners & dates):
- Aarti: Share representative prompt sets and 50 sample requests (anonymized) by 2029-02-15 so we can run the KV/prefix cache effectiveness study.
- DKim: Confirm retention policy and provide contact for security evidence (SOC2 owner) by 2029-02-16.
- Sean (Redwood): Deliver initial latency/throughput microbench report and recommended topology sketch by 2029-02-18.
- Irene (Redwood): Draft MSA/consumption model options and preliminary pricing ranges for Dedicated vs. Hosted by 2029-02-20.

Attachments: I attached the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the SLO matrix we sketched during the call.

If that matches your expectations I propose we lock the MAP and schedule the bench run for the week of 2029-02-19.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-map-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf), neptune-slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aarti Shah <aarti.shah@neptunehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, DKim Patel <dkpatel@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-11T20:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutually agreed next steps from today's deep-dive

Grace — thanks, this looks accurate and helpful. A couple of clarifications and confirmations: 

1) For the 60ms P95 target: this applies only to the routing endpoint (max prompt length 64 tokens). If the routing model failsover to the larger generator we expect a different SLO.
2) Batch summarization: the 1200 reqs/hour figure is a steady-state target for peak ingestion windows; during nightly backfills we could see short spikes to ~3k requests/hour, so we'd like to validate scaling behavior up to that level.
3) Security: I'll send the SOC contact (Meera Rao) and the anonymized sample requests by EOD 2029-02-15. We will likely need an on-prem option for audit log retention eventually — can you flag if that would change pricing materially?

Also +1 on the week of 2/19 for the bench run. We prefer early in the window (Mon/Tue).

Best,
Aarti
Director, Platform Engineering
Neptune Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aarti Shah <aarti.shah@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-12T02:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutually agreed next steps from today's deep-dive

Adding a few technical specifics on Redwood's proposed bench and topology so expectations are clear: 

- Bench plan: we will run two passes with your samples: (A) latency-focused single-shot workload with the 64-token routing patterns; (B) throughput-focused multi-worker batch test simulating 3k reqs/hour burst with 32-worker concurrency. Each pass will report P50/P95/P99 and CPU/GPU utilization traces, and KV cache hit rates.
- Topology sketch: for the production environment we recommend: edge short-route (us-west LB) -> regional dedicated pool (a mix of A100-80GB quantized hosts) -> persistent KV cache in-memory + a warm fallback pool on Redwood Hosted (cheaper instance type) to handle bursts.
- Failover behavior: if regional pool CPU exceeds 80% for >30s, traffic moves to hosted burst pool with rate-limited fallthrough.

I'll produce the bench script and the topology diagram (png) and drop them into the Drive folder by EOD 2/14. Grace — can you confirm whether Neptune's network team prefers VPC peering or a TLS-mutual auth endpoint for production? That will affect the runbook.

Sean
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
